newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China coal mining firm plans 170 mln B share IPO.
newsitem.headline: China coal mining firm plans 170 mln B share IPO.

text.p: China's Inner Mongolia Yitai Coal Co Ltd plans to make an intitial public offering of 170 million B shares in June 1997 but has not decided whether to list the stock in Shanghai or Shenzhen, a company official said on Monday.

The company, previously named Inner Mongolia Yikezhaomeng Coal Co Ltd, is among 33 domestic firms approved last December by the Securities Commission of the State Council as candidates to list B shares.

The firm will probably name China Guotai Securities Co as the domestic lead underwriter and Jardine Fleming International Inc as global coordinator, the official told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
Pricing and precise timing of the issue were not available.
Yitai plans to use the funds to mine coal and buy trains for transporting the coal.
Yitai estimated pre-tax profits of more than 100 million yuan for 1996, the official said, without providing comparative figures.
The company forecast output of 4.5-5.0 million tonnes of coal for 1997, compared with three million tonnes last year, he said.
Based in Dongsheng city in Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region where there are abundant coal resources, the firm supplies coal mainly to power stations and the smelting industry in east China.

After the B share issue, Yitai would have 370 million shares, consisting of 200 million legal person shares -- equity held by government-owned institutions that is non-tradeable under current regulations -- and 170 million B shares.
